contracts: dependency validity is independent of NovaOryn IDE release version
dependency fingerprint is derived from dependency declarations
installed Theia/Electron verification and dependency-state stamping are one operation
successful dependency verification continues into the remaining build pipeline
release: Dependency verifier control-flow and stale-state correction
checks: StampDependencies is a declared valid build-state action.
VerifyDependencies validates installed Electron and @theia/electron directly from the staged npm workspace.
Dependency-state matching excludes the application release version and uses a dependency fingerprint instead.
A release-only version bump does not force npm dependency reinstallation.
Build reuses an existing verified npm dependency tree when dependency declarations are unchanged.
Build captures the VerifyDependencies PowerShell exit code immediately and continues to CA/security/TypeScript/Theia verification on success.
Completed build-state validation still requires the current NovaOryn IDE version.
